title: Functional Programming Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of functional programming fundamentals using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates functional programming fundamentals.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Functional Programming Fundamentals** as part of **Functional Programming and Idiomatic Kotlin**. Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions. Use the subtopics—Pure Functions, Referential Transparency, Side Effects and Their Trade-offs—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with pure functions. Then compare it with referential transparency. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Pure Functions
items.text: Pure Functions describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Referential Transparency
items.text: Referential Transparency is one part of functional programming fundamentals. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Functional Programming Fundamentals removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
